extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, patent examiners and supervisors, patent practitioners and firm/IP management
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended criteria for improving patent examination quality, examiner/supervisor performance, prosecution practices, and related PTO pilots and metrics. Covers how to review, measure, train, and change procedures across examination, RCEs, interviews, restrictions, appeals, and allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supervisor-identified rejections in performance review
rubrics_metrics.description: Operator rejections identified by Supervisors should be tracked and used for examiner performance review; factor into count system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track supervisory-identified rejections as part of examiner metrics and incorporate into production/credit systems so supervisors' findings affect examiner evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-promotion-or-retirement expectation for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner does not qualify to be a supervisory examiner within reasonable time should examiner be retired?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider setting a reasonable advancement timeline and retirement/removal policy for examiners who do not progress to supervisory ranks to preserve quality and capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include supervisors in result metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Result metrics should include supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance metrics and accountability should apply to supervisors as well as examiners (e.g., review outcomes, reversals, pendency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor review of key office actions before mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors should review O/A, restriction requirements, final rejection, allowance and examiners answer on appeal before mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require supervisory review of initial and critical actions to ensure correctness before issuance; balance against added pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate Quality Review after first Office Action and post-RCE first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiate Quality review after first O/A, and first O/A following RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use early checkpoints (first action and first action after RCE) to detect issues early and guide examiner training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Quality Review on 35 U.S.C. §132(a) and 37 CFR §1.104 (Compact Prosecution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus Quality review on 35 U.S.C. §132(a) and 37 CFR §1.104 Requiring Compact Prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality reviews should emphasize legal sufficiency of rejections and the requirement to keep prosecution compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Quality Review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO should publish standards used for Quality Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make review criteria transparent so examiners and applicants understand the metrics and can improve practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use QIR to target outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use QIR to focus quality review on 'outliers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality Information Reports should highlight anomalous examiner behavior (high reversal rates, unusual pendency) for targeted review/training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce use of form-paragraph rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce use of form paragraph rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage boilerplate rejections that lack case-specific analysis; require individualized reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand examiner training on 35 U.S.C. 102(e) and PCT unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand Examiner training : 102 (e) and PCT unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide more training and examples on handling 102(e)-type art and unity/ restriction issues under PCT standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for confidential reporting of anomalous PTO personnel activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a mechanism by which anomalous activities by PTO personnel that adversely affect quality and/or pendency could be brought to PTO management attention for targeted training, without risk of negative consequences to the attorney or applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a confidential reporting/feedback channel so applicants/firms can report problematic examiner/SPE/OIPE conduct for corrective training rather than disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track supervisor contribution to pendency and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors add to pendency? : track actual examiner and Supervisor results‐ use it for performance management and training : QIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how supervisory reviews affect pendency and reversals; use data to optimize supervisory practices and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve examiner technical and language competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing the examiner's technical and English language linguistic understanding concerning the art would improve the quality of examiner determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in technical subject-matter and English-language training to reduce misunderstandings and erroneous rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit reliance on supervisory secondary review to avoid pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisory review of each O/A before it is sent out increases pendency; the objective should be to get it right the first time and not rely on back up reviews to catch mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage primary examiners to produce accurate first actions; use supervisory review selectively so as not to unduly increase pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appeals outcomes to identify examiners/supervisors needing improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use data concerning the affirmance or reversal of determinations made by individual examiners and their supervisors at the BPAI and Fed Circuit on the same art to identify which examiners and supervisors are doing higher quality work and areas for training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze BPAI/Federal Circuit reversal patterns by individual to target training for examiners/supervisors with high reversal rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain QIR data confidentiality and limit punitive use
rubrics_metrics.description: QIR data should be maintained by the PTO in confidence, not be made public to applicants, and should only be used to provide constructive feedback to examiners. It should not be used, except possibly in extreme circumstances, to penalize or terminate examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collected performance data primarily for development and training; protect examiner privacy and avoid routine punitive measures based on QIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and publish performance review metrics for examiners and supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and Publish Performance review metrics for Examiners and Supervisors: best practices; Conduct annual performance reviews according to standards: rank examiners and supervisors in art units according to performance as well as production; Address performance issues promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create transparent, standardized annual reviews that balance quality (reversal rates, compliance) with production and address underperformance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring program for remote and junior examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentoring for hotelling examiners; mentoring program could facilitate enhanced interactions between more experienced and junior Examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement formal mentoring (especially with remote/hotelling work) and provide merit-based incentives for experienced examiners to mentor juniors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to address attorney/agent performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop mechanism to address attorney/agent performance – PTO mechanism to inform law firm or corporation of attorney/agent performance: best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide non-disciplinary feedback channels to notify firms of practitioner performance issues and encourage targeted training at firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider public or firm-available metrics for attorney/agent performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Would Quality improve if performance data of attorneys and agents were public? – What is track record of attorney/agent? – What is attorney/agent’s pendency? – Frequency that attorney/agent utilizes RCEs – Result metrics : allowances, appeals, litigated claims – Data could incent attorneys/agents to improve performance: best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect metrics (pendency, RCE frequency, allowances, appeals) for practitioners; consider whether to share with firms or public to incentivize quality, but weigh confidentiality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO feedback to firms about practitioner performance
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO feedback to firms re attorney/agent performance; anomalous activities by practitioners could be brought to their attention and/or firm's management for performance management and targeted training, without rising to PTO disciplinary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage direct, constructive communications between examiners and firm management to improve practitioner conduct in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt unity of invention (PCT/EPO) and examine all claims presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Move to unity of invention under PCT/EPO; Examine all claims when presented: eliminate piecemeal search and examination‐ reduce pendency, eliminate serial examination and double patenting; Limit number of restrictions/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt examination standards closer to PCT/EPO unity to reduce restriction requirements and avoid serial divisional prosecution; limit restrictions per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust examiner counts/time for searching all claims at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate additional time required for examiner to search and examine all claims at time of filing and modify count system/per case accordingly: overall less time than serial search and exam of all divisional applications separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tiered count credits/time allocations so examiners are incentivized to perform comprehensive initial searches of all claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require presentation of all possible grounds for rejection in first Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: All possible grounds for rejection should be presented in the first Office action ‐ not emerge after applicant overcomes the stated rejection; Examiners who save references for subsequent actions on same claim should be penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action should be thorough and include all relevant references/grounds to avoid serial shifting of grounds that prolong prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit number of restriction requirements and provide clear species groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should be limited in the number of restriction requirements issued; Applicant should in every instance be given clearly enumerated species and claims groupings to choose from; species restriction for each invention group should be provided with first restriction Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce multiple restriction/ election practices that fragment prosecution; require clarity in species/group enumerations and include species restrictions at first restriction action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleconference and cure period for formal non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner believes applicant’s response is non compliant for any formal reason, examiner should initiate teleconference with applicant within 30 days of receipt of response and provide applicant with explanation for non compliance; Applicant should be given 30 days from teleconference to correct non compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use early communication to allow applicant correction of formal defects rather than issuing non-compliant rejections that prolong prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand First Office Action Interview pilot and related practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand PTO pilot program for first office action interviews: successfully leading to early allowances: Expand pilot to all art units; Identify situations where interview unsuccessful‐ improve interview process; Examiner production credit for interview; Examiners must be available for interviews (in person or by phone); Supervisors should participate when examiners lack signatory authority; Allow attorneys in firm to participate; Interviews should be collaborative: identify allowable subject matter and potential claim amendments; Agreements reached at interview should be honored: binding; All RCEs should have interview before first action within 30 days of RCE filing; Provide applicants with interview guidance/education; Monitor examiner performance regarding interview success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden and refine first-action interview pilots, ensure appropriate production credit to change examiner incentives, make interviews binding and collaborative, and monitor outcomes to measure efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify First Action Interview stage and credits to encourage early substantive engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Refocus the First Action Interview pilot to a stage prior to the examiners search and preliminary opinion might be more beneficial, assuming appropriate credit could be given. Such a pilot would allow applicant to inform the examiner on the invention and applicant’s view of the scope of the claims prior to the examiner searching and examining the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider giving production credit for substantive advancement rather than merely issuing an action; early-stage interviews before search could improve focus and reduce later rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure pilot effectiveness by actions-per-disposal and pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare number of actions per disposal in applications that utilize the first action interview pilot to those examined in the normal course; measure effect on pendency and number of allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze metrics (actions-per-disposal, time-to-allowance) by art unit to evaluate pilot effectiveness and adjust scope/eligibility accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide differentiated examination options by application complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore different examination procedures for applications of differing complexity; Applicants could choose a fast track option providing expedited prosecution with commensurate scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicants to opt into examination tracks based on complexity (references cited, claim scope/number), with corresponding count/time allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider allowing multiple dependent claims aligned with other offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider allowing use of multiple dependent claims that are in alignment with other patent offices, such as the European Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt multiple-dependent-claim practices to reduce the number of claims examined while preserving broad coverage options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve guidance and training on secondary considerations and functional limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt improved guidelines for examiners to handle secondary considerations and provide additional training and examples for functional limitations tied to specific structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples and training so examiners appropriately weigh secondary considerations (commercial success, copying, skepticism, etc.) and give proper weight to functional limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce double patenting rejections where low utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should be relieved of the obligation to make exhaustive double-patenting searches in many cases; one option would be to request a terminal disclaimer in every prosecution and search only if the Applicant refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procedural shifts (e.g., default terminal disclaimer) to reduce examiner time spent on double patenting when unlikely to benefit public given term limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trilateral/examining-office file sharing and deference to ISA work
rubrics_metrics.description: Trilateral office examiners should have common database with full file history of counterpart applications; How often does USPTO, examining a national-stage application from a PCT, give full faith and credit to its own work, allowing a case if it was treated favorably in the ISA/US written opinion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve work-sharing and access to counterpart file histories; give appropriate weight to ISA/ISA written opinions to avoid duplicative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivize abandonment of uninterested PCT national phase cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentives to abandon PCT national phase applications in which applicants have lost interest should be established to eliminate wasted time used in generating unnecessary office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cost or refund mechanisms to encourage express abandonment of unwanted national-phase filings to conserve examiner resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on when second rejection should be final and post-final handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When should second rejection over same reference be Final and when should amendment after final be considered? Is there an appealable issue or could more discussion resolve or close issue and prevent RCE?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop clear policy on when to make a rejection final, when to suggest amendments after final, and when to allow further prosecution instead of pushing applicants to RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require examiner to suggest amendments in final rejection to place claims in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Should examiner be required to suggest claim amendments in final rejection that would place claims in condition for allowance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requiring examiners to identify reasonable amendment paths in final rejections to facilitate closure without RCE/appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 132 declarations and accept rebuttal evidence post-final or on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Should 132 declarations be considered as of right after final? The Office should be willing to accept rebuttal evidence in the form of declarations submitted after a final rejection or as part of the appeal process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-evaluate strict prohibitions on after-final evidence/declarations and permit consideration where appropriate to avoid unnecessary RCEs or appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and analyze final rejection withdrawal data and reduce examiner counts accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejection data by art unit – Should examiner count be reduced when final rejection is withdrawn or when RCE is subsequently allowed without substantial claim amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QIR to track instances where finals are withdrawn; adjust production credits if finals are routinely withdrawn or allowances follow RCEs with minimal amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require substantive rebuttal by examiner for after-final amendments/responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response after final is entered (usually because it includes no claim amendments or new evidence), the Examiner usually just goes through the motions. At a minimum, the Examiner should be required to provide specific rebuttal of an applicant's arguments on the merits if an amendment is entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand specific, substantive examiner explanations for rejecting after-final arguments or amendments rather than perfunctory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use post-final conferences/interviews with SPE/ombudsman/BPAI member to reduce appeals/RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Move pre-appeal conference to conference after final rejection: include a member of Appeal board or ombudsman; post final interview/conference with the examiner, the SPE, an ombudsman or member of the BPAI could help increase percentage of amendments after final that place claims in condition for allowance and reduce appeals and RCEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement post-final, pre-appeal conferences with independent reviewers to identify amendment paths and reduce unnecessary appeals/RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and track new grounds for rejection on appeal and allowance rates after appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and track instances of 'new grounds for rejection' on appeal (new art or new statute); How frequent is allowance after filing of appeal brief?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect metrics on new grounds at appeal and allowance-after-appeal rates to identify problematic examiner practices and appeal-stage issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider eliminating Notice of Appeal and continuation-in-part applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Should notice of appeal be eliminated? Eliminate continuation in part applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate procedural changes that might reduce delay and manipulation of prosecution timelines (consider statutory/regulatory implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Pre-Appeal Brief Conference pilot as formal quality checkpoint and collect detailed metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Pre-Appeal Brief Conference and Appeal Brief Conference as formal quality check points, with formal collection, analysis, and compilation of quality analysis of the rejections presented for review. Collect data on outcomes, reopenings, allowances, pendency, usage rates, and technology-center breakdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically analyze pilot outcomes (percent avoiding appeals, reopenings, allowances) by TC and over time; compare pendency and actions-per-disposal for pilot vs non-pilot cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect pre-appeal pilot metrics including usage trend and impact on pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics: number/percentage of applications reopened or allowed as result of pre-appeal, broken down by Technology Center; average pendency comparison; number of pilot-eligible applicants that took advantage; trend of usage; total number of pre-appeal requests minus number of new non-final office actions and allowances immediately following the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track these metrics to evaluate pilot efficacy and tailor program to maximize impact; analyze cases that did not go on to appeal to understand changes enabling closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate root causes for filing RCEs and provide differentiated RCE handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the Causes for Filing RCEs; gather information on root causes and devise efficient ways to address different issues (e.g., RCEs filed solely to cite new prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify RCEs by cause and develop tailored procedures (e.g., expedited resolution paths for RCEs that only cite new art and contain no amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely examination and examiner continuity for RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine RCE within 1 month of filing; Maintain same examiner on RCE as original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce delay and case handoffs by prompt RCE handling and preserving examiner continuity to improve efficiency and reduce re-learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 'purgatory' RCEs requiring fee and request to resume examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Purgatory RCE’s: RCE to remain unexamined until applicant pays fee and requests continued prosecution: Is this a good idea?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procedural options to let applicants pause/resume RCEs to prioritize resources, balanced against applicants' rights and statutory timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid production credit for low-effort RCE allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is little or no work needed to allow a case on an RCE, no production credit should be given. One measure is the character of amendments made after an RCE and before the case is allowed; if amendments are minimal, no production credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust incentive systems so examiners are not rewarded for pushing cases into RCEs when allowance requires little new work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivize applicants to reduce unnecessary continuations via fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees that increase with the number of continuing applications (RCEs, Continuations, etc.) would provide incentives without eliminating an applicant’s right to file continuations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider graduated fee structures to discourage serial continuations while preserving statutory rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and clear reasons for allowance (MPEP 1302.14 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s statement of reasons for allowance should be comprehensive and clear. Reasons for allowance should not introduce unsupported claim limitations or broadening language not of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allowing claims, examiners must identify how claim elements distinguish over prior art, priority dates for claim elements in continuations/CIPs, interpretive statements (preamble/functional language), and identify file-history estoppel (amendments/arguments forming basis for allowance). Continue to review allowances for correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify priority date and prosecution interpretations in allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify priority date for each claim element in continuing and continuation in part applications; Examiner should state the interpretation given in prosecution to claim preamble and any field of use or functional terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly record prosecution positions and priority support to provide clarity to the public and reduce later disputes over claim scope.
